### `openadapt-flow qualify`

```text
Qualify: before a compiled workflow may run unattended on a real system, run it against the normal case and deliberate faults, and confirm it is verified by reading back the system of record and halts on every fault.

usage: openadapt-flow qualify <bundle> --verify verify.yaml [--cases ...] [--out DIR] [--certify [POLICY]] [--run-params FILE]
       openadapt-flow qualify <command> ...

The faults are a duplicated save button, a relabeled save button, a blanked
screen, and a weak or missing check that the write happened. Certifying
(--certify) signs the result under a policy such as clinical-write; you get a
signed report and a certified bundle the runner will admit. A certificate
covers only the environment the workflow was qualified in.

Definitions of qualify and certify:
  https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/#qualify
Certification policies (built-in clinical-write and permissive, or your own
YAML file passed to --certify):
  https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/#certification-policy
How to write verify.yaml:
  https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/QUALIFY_A_WORKFLOW.md

positional arguments:
  {campaign,schema,label,init,propose,accept,admit-local,from-demo,inspect,explain,report,set-identity,set-risk,trust-runner,set-effect,business-decision,judgment-cases,add-case,run,run-case,drills,add-requalification,certify}
    campaign            Qualify a bundle from verify.yaml (also the default form: `qualify
                        <bundle> --verify verify.yaml`)
    schema              Print the qualification-project JSON Schema
    label               Optionally set, remove, or list presentation-only entity labels
    init                Initialize a bundle's qualification project
    propose             Draft application, environment, identity, and effect pins from the
                        compiled demo. Missing pins HALT; nothing is guessed. Runs the proposed
                        oracle against a --break-it fault.
    accept              Confirm every proposed pin in one command after the proposed oracle
                        catches a --break-it fault. Refusing a pin HALTs.
    admit-local         Sign a local-dev admission for an accepted proposal. The signer cannot
                        enter a production trust map.
    from-demo           Propose pins from the demo, accept them, and optionally sign a local-dev
                        admission. After record and compile.
    inspect             Inspect qualification coverage
    explain             Explain qualification coverage
    report              Report qualification coverage
    set-identity        Set exact/normalized identity fields and their quorum
    set-risk            Confirm an action's reviewed business-risk classification
    trust-runner        Trust an Ed25519 qualification-runner public key
    set-effect          Assign verification-strength tier to an existing effect
    business-decision   Add, update, or inspect one reviewed finite business decision without
                        editing the workflow manifest
    judgment-cases      Store or check reviewed local judgment cases; this command never
                        synthesizes an executable rule from examples
    add-case            Add a representative or fault case
    run                 Import case results produced by the Desktop/local/customer-controlled
                        qualification runner
    run-case            Run one current qualification case (the practice item or a readiness
                        drill) with Flow-owned Standard authorization
    drills              Add the five readiness drills for the practice case's save and trust this
                        computer's local drill key (a local campaign)
    add-requalification
                        Add a condition that requires this workflow to be requalified
    certify             Persist a combined qualification and existing-policy decision

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `openadapt-flow qualify campaign`

```text
Qualify: before a compiled workflow may run unattended on a real system, run it against the normal case and deliberate faults, and confirm it is verified by reading back the system of record and halts on every fault.

usage: openadapt-flow qualify <bundle> --verify verify.yaml [--cases ...] [--out DIR] [--certify [POLICY]] [--run-params FILE]
       openadapt-flow qualify <command> ... campaign
       [-h] --verify YAML [--cases CASE [CASE ...]] [--trials TRIALS] [--out DIR]
       [--certify [POLICY]] [--run-params JSON] [--campaign-id CAMPAIGN_ID]
       bundle

The faults are a duplicated save button, a relabeled save button, a blanked
screen, and a weak or missing check that the write happened. Certifying
(--certify) signs the result under a policy such as clinical-write; you get a
signed report and a certified bundle the runner will admit. A certificate
covers only the environment the workflow was qualified in.

Definitions of qualify and certify:
  https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/#qualify
Certification policies (built-in clinical-write and permissive, or your own
YAML file passed to --certify):
  https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/#certification-policy
How to write verify.yaml:
  https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/QUALIFY_A_WORKFLOW.md

positional arguments:
  bundle                Compiled workflow bundle directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --verify YAML         verify.yaml: the per-workflow read-back, field mapping, save step and
                        inputs
  --cases CASE [CASE ...]
                        Run only these cases (representative, fault-ambiguity, fault-wrong-
                        identity, fault-stale-identity, fault-weak-effect, fault-missing-effect).
                        Certification needs all six.
  --trials TRIALS       Trials per case (default: verify.yaml, 3)
  --out DIR             New output directory
  --certify [POLICY]    Certify under this policy (default: campaign.policy in verify.yaml,
                        usually clinical-write). See
                        https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/#certification-policy.
  --run-params JSON     After certifying, run the certified bundle once with these inputs
  --campaign-id CAMPAIGN_ID
                        Campaign id (default: verify.yaml or generated)
```

### `openadapt-flow qualify run-case`

```text
usage: openadapt-flow qualify <bundle> --verify verify.yaml [--cases ...] [--out DIR] [--certify [POLICY]] [--run-params FILE]
       openadapt-flow qualify <command> ... run-case
       [-h] --case-id CASE_ID --inputs JSON --campaign-id CAMPAIGN_ID --run-id RUN_ID
       [--qualification-campaign-authority-file PATH] --run-dir RUN_DIR [--url URL] [--headed]
       [--dry-run] [--fault-driver NAME] [--backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}]
       [--agent-url URL] [--macos-app APP] [--macos-window-title TITLE] [--linux-app APP]
       [--linux-window-title TITLE] [--linux-allow-physical-input] [--rdp-host HOST]
       [--rdp-window OWNER] [--rdp-window-title TITLE] [--rdp-readiness-text TEXT]
       [--allow-surface-override] [--browser-cdp-endpoint URL] [--browser-page-url URL]
       [--config YAML] [--effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}]
       [--effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL] [--effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT] [--api-actuator]
       [--api-base-url API_BASE_URL] [--durable] [--approver-policy FILE] [--approver-webhook URL]
       [--approver-webhook-id APPROVER_WEBHOOK_ID] [--approver-webhook-kind {agent,system}]
       [--approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}] [--approval-wait SECONDS]
       bundle

positional arguments:
  bundle                Sealed workflow bundle directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --case-id CASE_ID     Declared practice case or readiness drill
  --inputs JSON         Private canonical runtime-input artifact from Desktop (mode 0600; params
                        and worklists only)
  --campaign-id CAMPAIGN_ID
                        Local campaign identity
  --run-id RUN_ID       One local case-attempt identity
  --qualification-campaign-authority-file PATH
                        Private owner-only signed non-production authority for this exact trial;
                        required once the run actuates under a campaign permit
  --run-dir RUN_DIR     New durable case-attempt directory
  --url URL             Target app URL
  --headed              Run browser headed
  --dry-run             Validate without input
  --fault-driver NAME   A drill's fault driver from the openadapt_flow.qualification_fault_drivers
                        entry point (a configured campaign). Without it, a drill uses this
                        computer's local drill campaign (see `qualify drills`).
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. TextEdit). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --browser-cdp-endpoint URL
                        Run in an already-running, signed-in local Chromium through its loopback
                        DevTools endpoint (for example, http://127.0.0.1:9222) instead of
                        launching a new, signed-out browser. The run binds the one open tab on the
                        --url origin, starts from the screen it shows, and never navigates or
                        closes the browser. Overrides backend.browser_cdp_endpoint from --config.
  --browser-page-url URL
                        Exact current URL of the tab to run in, when more than one open tab has
                        the --url origin. Requires --browser-cdp-endpoint.
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML wiring backend / actuation / effects / runtime /
                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
                        System-of-record EffectVerifier to wire so consequential writes are
                        verified against the real record (not the screen). The sql/file kinds need
                        their config fields (sql_query, root, ...) from a --config deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT
                        Document-store root for the document-hash effect verifier
  --api-actuator        Wire the API/tool actuation tier: a step carrying an ApiBinding is
                        performed via the API (deterministic, $0) and confirmed by the effect
                        verifier, skipping the GUI
  --api-base-url API_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the API actuator (implies --api-actuator)
  --durable             Enable the Tier-3 durable runtime: checkpoint each verified step and
                        durably PAUSE on halt, so the run is resumable via `resume` (never re-
                        performing a confirmed write)
  --approver-policy FILE
                        An openadapt.approver-policy/v1 JSON file: which kinds of approver
                        (person, rule, agent, system) may answer each class of save. Without it
                        only a person may answer. A clinical_write save takes a non-person
                        approver only when the policy pins an opt-in.
  --approver-webhook URL
                        Ask this https endpoint (the customer's approver agent or system) about
                        each waiting save, with HMAC-signed, PHI-free messages. The secret is read
                        from OPENADAPT_APPROVER_WEBHOOK_SECRET. A person can still answer in
                        Desktop. Needs --approver-webhook-id and a policy that allows the
                        approver's kind.
  --approver-webhook-id APPROVER_WEBHOOK_ID
                        The webhook approver's opaque id, such as system:acme-approvals
  --approver-webhook-kind {agent,system}
                        Whether the webhook approver is an agent or a system (default system)
  --approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}
                        Per-item approval before each consequential save. each_item (the default
                        for every run): the run waits before every save until a person approves it
                        in Desktop's Run it (see `item-approval`). problems_only: only problems go
                        to a person; until a switch record is configured, every save still asks.
                        not_gated: no per-item pause, recorded in the report (the hosted runner,
                        Execute and MCP callers). Overrides runtime.approval_mode. A resume always
                        keeps the run's own mode.
  --approval-wait SECONDS
                        How long the run waits for a person's answer before it stops before the
                        save (default 900, at most 14400). An answer given later can still be used
                        by `resume`.
```

### `openadapt-flow repair`

```text
usage: openadapt-flow repair [-h]
                             {register,list,show,review,campaign,approve,stage,canary,canary-record,rollback,status}
                             ...

positional arguments:
  {register,list,show,review,campaign,approve,stage,canary,canary-record,rollback,status}
    register            Register a (prior, proposed) bundle pair as a repair candidate; refuses
                        (fail closed) any contract weakening without a new qualification revision
    list                List candidates and their lifecycle states
    show                Show a candidate's reviewable diff, campaigns, and state
    review              Record a human review of the candidate's diff
    campaign            Run a campaign against the candidate's evidence frames: 'replay' (healthy
                        drift battery must all pass) or 'fault' (ambiguity / wrong-entity / stale-
                        target / dialog / verifier-failure frames must all be REFUSED)
    approve             HUMAN approval gating promotion; refuses unless the diff was reviewed and
                        BOTH campaigns passed. Binds the exact bundle hashes
    stage               Copy BOTH bundles into the store by content hash and re-verify them byte-
                        exact (prior too, so rollback is always local)
    canary              Atomically activate the staged bundle in CANARY mode: a bounded first-N-
                        runs window with per-run verification before full active
    canary-record       Record one canary run from its run directory; any silent-incorrect or
                        verification regression auto-reverts to the prior bundle
    rollback            One-command rollback: restore the prior bundle hash as the active pointer
    status              Show the atomic active-bundle pointer and its lineage

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `openadapt-flow login`

```text
usage: openadapt-flow login [-h] [--token TOKEN] [--host HOST]
                            [--destination-kind {openadapt-managed,customer-managed,local}]
                            [--trusted-host TRUSTED_HOST] [--no-save] [--allow-plaintext-token]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --token TOKEN         Ingest token (oai_ingest_…). Falls back to OPENADAPT_INGEST_TOKEN, then OS
                        keychain, then an existing config migration token. Mint one at
                        <host>/dashboard/settings/ingest.
  --host HOST           Hosted base URL (default: config.toml host, else https://app.openadapt.ai)
  --destination-kind {openadapt-managed,customer-managed,local}
                        Trust class for the token destination
  --trusted-host TRUSTED_HOST
                        Exact allowed customer-managed origin (repeatable)
  --no-save             Validate only; do not store the host or token
  --allow-plaintext-token
                        Explicitly allow mode-0600 config token storage when no OS keychain is
```

### `openadapt-flow materialize-approved`

```text
usage: openadapt-flow materialize-approved [-h] --archive ARCHIVE --approval APPROVAL --out OUT
                                           [--expect-archive-sha256 EXPECT_ARCHIVE_SHA256]

Approval binds the archive's own SHA-256, so the archive cannot carry it and an archive unzipped
elsewhere reads as unapproved. This places the reviewer's existing approval record beside the
extracted bytes and then runs the unchanged approval gate. It approves nothing.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --archive ARCHIVE     Approved immutable archive (.approved.zip)
  --approval APPROVAL   Existing approval record: either the derivative's .openadapt-approval.json
                        or the openadapt.sanitization/v1 ingest envelope a deployment persisted
                        for it
  --out OUT             New, empty derivative directory to materialize
  --expect-archive-sha256 EXPECT_ARCHIVE_SHA256
                        Pin the archive to a digest the caller already trusts, checked
                        independently of the approval record
```

```text
options:
```

```text
  --recording RECORDING
                        Approved sanitized recording derivative used to compile the bundle
  --bundle BUNDLE       Approved sanitized bundle derivative whose exact archive will upload
  --run-dir RUN_DIR     Successful governed replay directory containing report.json
  --policy POLICY       Named or file-backed policy that the bundle must pass
  --risk-class {low,consequential}
                        Compiled workflow risk class: low for reversible-only workflows,
                        consequential when any step is irreversible; must match the bundle
  --environment ENVIRONMENT
                        Non-PHI validation environment identifier; only its SHA-256 is uploaded
  --target-kind {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Optional expected replay substrate. The signed value is derived from
                        report.json; a supplied value must match it exactly.
  --target-url TARGET_URL
                        Web only: exact non-PHI HTTPS entry URL used by the validated browser
                        workflow; required for web and refused for native/remote
  --allowed-host ALLOWED_HOST
                        Additional exact hostname the hosted browser may reach (repeatable); the
                        target hostname is included automatically
  --compiler-config COMPILER_CONFIG
                        Optional JSON object describing the compile configuration
  --out OUT             Attestation JSON output path
  --host HOST           Hosted base URL (default: configured host or https://app.openadapt.ai)
  --destination-kind {openadapt-managed,customer-managed,local}
                        Trust class for the challenge destination
  --trusted-host TRUSTED_HOST
                        Exact allowed customer-managed origin (repeatable)
  --token TOKEN         Ingest token used to acquire and sign the one-time challenge
```

```text
usage: openadapt-flow push [-h] [--kind {recording,bundle}] [--name NAME]

                           [--destination-kind {openadapt-managed,customer-managed,local}]

                           [--auto-approve] [--validation-attestation VALIDATION_ATTESTATION]
                           [--resolves-run-id RESOLVES_RUN_ID] [--host HOST] [--token TOKEN]
                           [--json]
                           [path]

positional arguments:

                        recording directory found under the current directory.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {recording,bundle}
                        What the directory is (default: recording)
  --name NAME           Workflow name (the server auto-suggests one otherwise)
  --workflow-id WORKFLOW_ID
                        Existing hosted workflow UUID to receive this validated bundle as a new
                        active version (bundle uploads only)
  --deployment-kind {cloud,byoc,regulated}
                        Execution deployment lane (independent of destination trust; default:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_DEPLOYMENT_KIND env, then config.toml deployment_lane, else
                        cloud). All lanes may upload only a verified sanitized derivative.
  --attest-non-phi      Deprecated and refused: declarations no longer bypass sanitization,
                        review, or exact-hash approval.
  --destination-kind {openadapt-managed,customer-managed,local}
                        Trust class for the upload endpoint. app.openadapt.ai is recognized
                        automatically; customer-managed endpoints also require --trusted-host.
  --trusted-host TRUSTED_HOST
                        Exact allowed customer-managed origin, e.g. https://control.example
                        (repeatable)
  --sanitized-out SANITIZED_OUT
                        Where to create the derivative when PATH is raw (default: OPENADAPT_HOME)
  --auto-approve        Administrator policy approval for fully covered, stable derivatives; human
                        review is the default.
  --validation-attestation VALIDATION_ATTESTATION
                        Challenge-bound runtime-validation JSON required for runnable bundles
  --resolves-run-id RESOLVES_RUN_ID
                        Halted run UUID resolved by this validated replacement; requires --kind
                        bundle and --workflow-id
  --host HOST           Hosted base URL (default: config.toml host, else https://app.openadapt.ai)
  --token TOKEN         Ingest token (default: OPENADAPT_INGEST_TOKEN env, OS keychain, then an
                        existing config migration token)
  --json                Emit one stable openadapt.push-result/v1 JSON object for Desktop and other
                        local controllers
```

```text
                        DIR instead of contacting any host. The receipt is generated from a closed
                        allow-list -- closed enums, counts, digests, versions -- and can carry no
                        screenshot, OCR text, typed value, parameter, URL, hostname, coordinate,
                        or free-form text
```

### `openadapt-flow console`

```text
usage: openadapt-flow console [-h] [--bundles BUNDLES] [--runs RUNS] [--skills SKILLS]
                              [--port PORT] [--allow-actions] [--attend] [--url URL] [--headed]
                              [--allow-model-grounding] [--remote-decisions]
                              [--remote-decision-host URL]
                              [--backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}] [--agent-url URL]
                              [--macos-app APP] [--macos-window-title TITLE] [--linux-app APP]
                              [--linux-window-title TITLE] [--linux-allow-physical-input]
                              [--rdp-host HOST] [--rdp-window OWNER] [--rdp-window-title TITLE]
                              [--rdp-readiness-text TEXT] [--allow-surface-override]
                              [--config YAML]
                              [--effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}]
                              [--effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL] [--effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT]
                              [--api-actuator] [--api-base-url API_BASE_URL] [--durable]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --bundles BUNDLES     Directory scanned (2 levels deep) for workflow bundle directories
                        (default: current directory)
  --runs RUNS           Directory scanned for run directories (default: runs/)
  --skills SKILLS       Extra directory scanned for skill libraries (skills.json); the bundles
                        directory is always scanned too
  --port PORT           Port on 127.0.0.1 (the bind address is loopback-only, always)
  --allow-actions       Enable executing governed actions (approve / resume / certify / promote /
                        rollback) from the UI after an explicit confirm that shows the exact
                        command. Default: read-only — the UI renders the command for the operator
                        to copy instead
  --attend              Open the authenticated local Needs Attention queue first. It is read-only
                        unless --allow-actions is also supplied; attended mutations additionally
                        require an engine-issued pause capability and qualified deployment service
  --url URL             Live browser URL for attended verification/continuation. Required for
                        --backend web unless backend.url is set in --config.
  --headed              Keep the attended browser visible for the operator. The web attended-
                        action path requires a headed session.
  --allow-model-grounding
                        EGRESS OPT-IN: permit configured off-box model components during fresh
                        attended verification and deterministic continuation
  --remote-decisions    Publish open attended pauses to the hosted decision surface over an
                        OUTBOUND-ONLY connection, so a paired phone can answer them from anywhere
                        without any inbound port, certificate, or reverse proxy. Requires --attend
                        --allow-actions, a --config whose human_decisions.remote is enabled with
                        an exact tenant and runner, and OPENADAPT_RUNNER_TOKEN. Only the PHI-free
                        signed task and the closed halt context cross the wire; screenshots never
                        leave
  --remote-decision-host URL
                        Hosted control-plane origin for --remote-decisions (default: the
                        configured hosted host, https://app.openadapt.ai)
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. TextEdit). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML wiring backend / actuation / effects / runtime /
                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
                        System-of-record EffectVerifier to wire so consequential writes are
                        verified against the real record (not the screen). The sql/file kinds need
                        their config fields (sql_query, root, ...) from a --config deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT
                        Document-store root for the document-hash effect verifier
  --api-actuator        Wire the API/tool actuation tier: a step carrying an ApiBinding is
                        performed via the API (deterministic, $0) and confirmed by the effect
                        verifier, skipping the GUI
  --api-base-url API_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the API actuator (implies --api-actuator)
  --durable             Enable the Tier-3 durable runtime: checkpoint each verified step and
                        durably PAUSE on halt, so the run is resumable via `resume` (never re-
                        performing a confirmed write)
```

```text
                     ~/.openadapt/jit)
```

```text
usage: openadapt-flow jit review [-h] [--key-dir KEY_DIR] [--principal PRINCIPAL]
```

## openadapt agent

### `openadapt-agent`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent [-h] [--version] {serve,repair,authoring,emit-skill,seal} ...

Your AI agent decides what to enter. OpenAdapt enters it in the app and checks that it saved.
'serve' with no flags starts a sandbox.

positional arguments:
  {serve,repair,authoring,emit-skill,seal}
    serve               Serve workflows to your AI agent over MCP (stdio). With no flags, serve
                        the sandbox.
    repair              Control whether calling agents may help repair halted runs (local only).
    authoring           Hosted authoring mailbox client (ChatGPT.com / Claude.ai). Outbound HTTPS
                        only; not an HTTP listener.
    emit-skill          Write an Agent Skill for one workflow: what it does, its inputs, and how
                        to read the result. No recorded values, step text, or secrets.
    seal                Pin OpenAdapt Cloud's Seal keys and verify a Seal offline.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
```

### `openadapt-agent serve`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent serve [-h] [--mode {sandbox,attended,production}] [--bundles BUNDLES]
                             [--sandbox-engine {auto,flow,simulated}] [--authoring]
                             [--windows-agent-url URL] [--remote-window APP]
                             [--remote-window-title TITLE] [--citrix]
                             [--authoring-screens {off,scrubbed,unscrubbed}] [--tutorial]
                             [--allow-run] [--allow-protected-export]
                             [--allow-synthetic-recorded-defaults] [--allow-attended-actions]
                             [--url URL] [--config YAML] [--policy NAME-OR-PATH]
                             [--runs-dir RUNS_DIR] [--timeout SECONDS]
                             [--approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}]
                             [--delegate-approvals AGENT_ID] [--allow-url-override]
                             [--flow-cli FLOW_CLI] [--headed] [--allow-model-grounding]
                             [--extra-run-arg ARG] [--repair-access FILE] [--repair-dir DIR]
                             [--hold-on-halt SECONDS]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --mode {sandbox,attended,production}
                        sandbox (default with no --bundles): one synthetic workflow that shows
                        every result. production: run the compiled workflows in --bundles.
                        attended: production plus decisions on paused runs by a person at this
                        computer. --bundles without --mode stays read-only.
  --bundles BUNDLES     Bundle directory: either one compiled bundle, or a directory whose
                        immediate subdirectories are bundles. Needed for --mode production and
                        --mode attended.
  --sandbox-engine {auto,flow,simulated}
                        Advanced. flow drives the synthetic app in a hidden browser (needs the
                        tutorial extra); simulated returns the same results without opening it.
                        auto picks flow when it can.
  --authoring           Register first-demo authoring tools over local stdio: observe,
                        start_record, click, halt. Local Claude Code path is the first authoring
                        UI. Pass --url --headed to pin Playwright Chromium with empty cookies;
                        pause_for_input is how a person signs in there. --url is not the Chrome
                        window you already signed into. Omit --url to pin a unique frontmost
                        Chrome window after login (macOS; no DOM identity). Local stdio may also
                        type through the recorder; hosted MCP remains pause-only. Does not enable
                        run tools. This process stays stdio and must not be served over HTTP.
  --windows-agent-url URL
                        With --authoring: drive a native Windows app through the Flow Windows
                        agent server running on the Windows computer (for example
                        http://localhost:5001, or an SSH-forwarded port from another computer).
                        The agent's input goes through the same synthetic-input path replay uses.
                        The token comes from OAFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN.
  --remote-window APP   With --authoring: drive the RDP or Citrix session shown in this local
                        client window (app name, for example 'Microsoft Remote Desktop'). Screen-
                        only: the agent clicks pixels and presses keys.
  --remote-window-title TITLE
                        With --remote-window or --citrix: pick one window by its title.
  --citrix              With --authoring: drive the local Citrix Workspace window (--remote-window
                        overrides the app name). Screen-only.
  --authoring-screens {off,scrubbed,unscrubbed}
                        With --authoring: let the agent see the pinned window through the screen
                        tool, so it can drive a native Windows app or a remote session from
                        pixels. scrubbed removes identifiers first and shares nothing if that
                        fails. Default off.
  --tutorial            Older name for --mode sandbox. Synthetic only. Cannot be combined with
                        --bundles, --url, or --config.
  --allow-run           Older name for --mode production (with --bundles) or --mode sandbox
                        (without). Without a mode or this flag, --bundles stays read-only.
  --allow-protected-export
                        DANGER: export raw workflow labels, recorded values, intents, local paths,
                        reports, stdout, stderr, and exception detail to the MCP client. Off by
                        default; enable only for an explicitly trusted local client inside the
                        protected data boundary.
  --allow-synthetic-recorded-defaults
                        DEMO ONLY: let omitted workflow parameters reuse recorded values. Use only
                        with synthetic demonstrations; production requires every declared
                        parameter so a run cannot silently target the recorded customer or record.
  --allow-attended-actions
                        Part of --mode attended. Register governed Reject/Teach/Escalate tools for
                        signed durable pauses. With --config, also register Continue/Skip through
                        Flow's deployment-bound live verifier and deterministic resume path.
  --url URL             Target app URL passed to every `openadapt-flow run` (operator-fixed)
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML forwarded to `openadapt-flow run --config`
  --policy NAME-OR-PATH
                        Certifying policy forwarded to `openadapt-flow run --policy` and used by
                        get_workflow's certification check
  --runs-dir RUNS_DIR   Directory for run records and evidence (default:
                        $OPENADAPT_AGENT_RUNS_DIR, else ~/.openadapt/runs; the sandbox uses
                        ~/.openadapt/agent-sandbox). Never relative to the folder the client
                        starts the server in.
  --timeout SECONDS     Per-call timeout for each governed run (default: 600)
  --approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}
                        Per-save approval passed to every `openadapt-flow run`. Unset (the
                        default): Flow decides, and under the Standard and Regulated profiles each
                        save waits for approval (each_item); a run waiting for that approval
                        reports needs_review. not_gated turns the pause off for every run this
                        server starts, and each run's result and Flow's report record that.
                        Callers can't change it.
  --delegate-approvals AGENT_ID
                        Let the calling agent answer saves that wait for an approval, as the
                        opaque id AGENT_ID (for example agent:intake-bot). Adds the
                        list_approval_requests and answer_approval_request tools. Flow accepts the
                        agent's answer only where the run's approver policy (openadapt-flow run
                        --approver-policy) allows an agent for that step; by default only a person
                        may answer. Flow records the agent as the approver.
  --allow-url-override  Permit MCP callers to pass a per-call `url` argument (default: the target
                        URL is fixed by --url/--config at server start)
  --flow-cli FLOW_CLI   Command used to invoke the flow CLI (default: this interpreter's `python
                        -m openadapt_flow`, so the flow installed alongside this server is always
                        the one that runs); may contain spaces, e.g. 'openadapt-flow'
  --headed              Keep a deployment-configured attended web session visible to the local
                        operator (required for web Continue/Skip).
  --allow-model-grounding
                        Explicit CLI opt-in for configured off-box model grounding. A deployment
                        config may also opt in; otherwise verification remains local.
  --extra-run-arg ARG   Extra argument appended to every `openadapt-flow run` invocation
                        (repeatable; operator-fixed, e.g. --extra-run-arg=--allow-unencrypted for
                        a demo bundle)
  --repair-access FILE  Screen access setting for repairs, written by `openadapt-agent repair
                        access`. Without it, halted runs still return needs_repair but no screens,
                        and teach_repair is not offered.
  --repair-dir DIR      Where repair tokens, approvals, and candidates live (default
                        RUNS_DIR/.repair).
  --hold-on-halt SECONDS
                        With --repair-access, keep a halted browser run's page open this long so
                        teach_repair acts on it (default 300; 0 turns it off).
```

```text
positional arguments:
```

```text
process only makes outbound HTTPS.
```
